title: 育儿与教育：双语与多语养育 — Day 11

questions.question: 两个孩子学英文：甲 3 岁开始、5 岁中断；乙 7 岁开始、此后十年每天坚持互动输入。按语言习得的大样本证据，哪种判断最站得住？
options: 乙更可能更流利，预测最终流利度的是累积输入小时数而非起点
两人差不多，因为语法水平主要由天赋决定，与输入关系不大
甲更可能更流利，因为 7 岁前的语言关键期窗口一过就基本关闭了
甲口音更好、语法也更好，早开始在各方面都有不可逆的优势
questions.explanation: Hartshorne 等对 67 万人的研究显示语法窗口到约 17 岁才显著关闭，起点和持续输入是两个变量，真正预测流利度的是累积小时数。「7 岁前一刀切」是对关键期假说的通俗化误读；口音窗口确实更早，但不等于全面不可逆。
questions.question_en: Child A starts English at 3 and stops at 5; Child B starts at 7 and keeps up daily interactive input for ten years. Based on large-sample evidence on language acquisition, which judgment holds up best?
options_en: B is likely more fluent: cumulative hours of input, not the starting age, predict eventual fluency
They end up about the same, since grammar depends mainly on talent rather than input
A is likely more fluent, because the critical window essentially closes by age 7
A will have better accent and grammar, since an early start gives irreversible advantages across the board
questions.explanation_en: Hartshorne et al.'s study of 670,000 people found the grammar-learning window doesn't close sharply until around 17. Starting early and sustained input are separate variables, and cumulative hours are what predict fluency. The 'before age 7 or never' idea is a popularized misreading of the critical-period hypothesis; the accent window does close earlier, but that is not a blanket irreversibility.

questions.question: 一个家庭严格执行「一人一语」(OPOL)，孩子却越来越只说多数语言、拒绝弱势语言。按双语养育的研究，最该调整的是什么？
options: 尊重孩子的选择先暂停弱势语言，等他大一点、自己有兴趣了再重新开始
保持平日不变，改为周末集中说弱势语言，用整块时间弥补平时的不足
更严格地执行 OPOL，孩子一混用两种语言就立即纠正，避免语言混乱
提高弱势语言占孩子清醒时间的比例，并把它绑在共读、和祖辈视频这类高情感价值的活动上
questions.explanation: De Houwer 的调查显示 OPOL 下仍有约四分之一孩子只说多数语言；关键不在方法而在弱势语言的累积时长（低于约 20% 难以主动产出），并要刻意保护。混语是双语大脑的正常现象，不必紧张纠正；撤退会让弱势语言迅速消退，周末式策略输入量不够。
questions.question_en: A family strictly follows 'one parent, one language' (OPOL), yet the child increasingly speaks only the majority language and refuses the minority one. According to bilingual-parenting research, what most needs to change?
options_en: Respect the child's choice and pause the minority language until they are older and interested on their own
Keep weekdays as they are and concentrate the minority language on weekends to make up for the shortfall
Enforce OPOL more strictly and correct the child immediately whenever they mix languages, to avoid confusion
Raise the minority language's share of the child's waking hours and tie it to emotionally rich activities like shared reading or video calls with grandparents
questions.explanation_en: De Houwer found about a quarter of children in OPOL families still end up speaking only the majority language. What matters is cumulative exposure to the minority language (below roughly 20% it rarely becomes productive), and it has to be deliberately protected. Code-switching is normal for a bilingual brain; backing off lets the language fade fast; weekend-only strategies don't supply enough input.

questions.question: 关于让孩子坚持双语，哪种动机在证据上最稳、也最能长期维系孩子的意愿？
options: 双语能提升孩子的执行功能，这一优势已被多项大样本元分析反复证实
双语能提高孩子的智商，让他在学业竞争中跑得更快
双语让孩子能和只会这门语言的家人深谈，维系家庭与文化的连接
双语是未来升学和求职的硬通货，越早布局回报越高
questions.explanation: 「双语带来执行功能优势」在 Paap 等的大样本元分析中难以复制，拿它做卖点很不稳；而 Wong Fillmore 发现移民孩子失去母语后无法与祖辈深谈，语言流失就是关系流失。具体、不可替代的关系场景才是孩子主动学习的内在锚点。
questions.question_en: When it comes to keeping a child bilingual, which motivation is best supported by evidence and most likely to sustain the child's willingness over time?
options_en: Improved executive function, an advantage repeatedly confirmed by large meta-analyses
A higher IQ that helps the child get ahead in academic competition
Being able to talk deeply with family members who only speak that language, keeping the family and cultural connection alive
A hard currency for future admissions and jobs, with higher payoff the earlier you invest
questions.explanation_en: The claimed executive-function advantage has been hard to replicate in large meta-analyses such as Paap et al., so it is a shaky selling point. Wong Fillmore, by contrast, showed that immigrant children who lose their heritage language can no longer talk deeply with grandparents: language loss is relationship loss. A concrete, irreplaceable relationship is what anchors a child's own motivation.
